source:
Roblox Grand Strategy Game Design

Game Overview

Create a multiplayer grand strategy game set on a fictional continent based on the land shape of Europe. The coastlines, mountains, rivers, islands, and overall geography should resemble Europe so the map feels familiar, but none of the countries, borders, capitals, or cities should use real-world names. Everything should use placeholder names that can be replaced later.

The game should focus on expansion, diplomacy, economics, military strategy, and world conquest while remaining easy to learn and fast-paced.

A full match should last 45-90 minutes.

Main Menu

When players join, they enter a lobby.

From the lobby they can:

Choose a nation.

View nation information.

Invite friends.

Customize cosmetics.

Vote for game settings.

Wait for enough players before the match starts.

Nation Selection

There are 51 playable nations spread across the continent.

Every nation occupies a unique location on the map.

Players select a nation before the match begins.

Each nation displays:

Placeholder Country Name

Flag (Placeholder)

Difficulty

Starting Economy

Population

Resources

National Bonus

Example:

Country 01

Capital:
Capital Alpha

Cities:

City Alpha

City Beta

City Gamma

City Delta

Country 02

Capital:
Capital Bravo

Cities:

City Echo

City Delta

City Sierra

City Omega

Every country should only use placeholder names until custom names are created later.

No real country names should appear anywhere.

Spawning

Once every player has selected a nation and the countdown ends:

Players automatically load into their nation's capital city.

The capital acts as the center of government.

Every capital contains:

Government Building

Barracks

Factory

Town Hall

Resource Storage

Spawn Point

Airport (locked early game)

Rail Station

Construction Yard

Players may freely walk around the capital while also controlling their nation through the strategy interface.

Map Design

The world is a fictional continent inspired by Europe.

The map should include:

Northern frozen regions

Western islands

Large mountain ranges

Central plains

Southern peninsulas

Eastern forests

Major rivers

Large lakes

Surrounding oceans

Although the terrain resembles Europe, every border is fictional.

No real borders should be copied exactly.

Provinces

Each nation contains several provinces.

Each province includes:

Population

Income

Infrastructure

Natural Resources

Defense

Happiness

Some provinces contain cities.

Others are farmland or wilderness.

Capturing provinces expands national territory.

Capitals

Every nation starts with exactly one capital.

The capital:

Produces the highest income.

Contains government buildings.

Acts as the nation's respawn point.

Stores national resources.

Can recruit every military unit.

If a capital is captured:

Production decreases.

National morale drops.

Income is reduced.

If the capital is recaptured, these penalties are removed.

Cities

Each nation contains multiple cities besides the capital.

City names are placeholders only.

Example city names:

City Alpha

City Bravo

City Charlie

City Delta

City Echo

City Foxtrot

City Gamma

City Nova

City Orion

City Zenith

These names are temporary and intended to be replaced during later development.

National Bonuses

Each nation begins with one randomly assigned or pre-designed bonus.

Examples include:

Industrial Nation

Military Tradition

Scientific Excellence

Trade Specialists

Agricultural Experts

Mining Efficiency

Engineering Experts

Economic Growth

These bonuses help make each nation feel unique.

Economy

Money is earned from:

Taxes

Cities

Factories

Trade

Resources

The player spends money on:

Buildings

Military

Technology

Infrastructure

Diplomacy

Espionage

Repairs

Resources

Resources generate automatically.

Types include:

Food

Steel

Oil

Coal

Stone

Wood

Gold

Rare Materials

Different provinces specialize in different resources.

Buildings

Players construct:

Factories

Research Centers

Military Bases

Farms

Power Plants

Harbors

Airfields

Hospitals

Police Stations

Fortresses

Buildings upgrade through multiple levels.

Higher levels greatly improve production.

Military

Military branches include:

Infantry

Mechanized Infantry

Heavy Infantry

Engineers

Tanks

Rocket Vehicles

Special Forces

Aircraft

Naval Fleets

Support Vehicles

Each unit has strengths and weaknesses.

Armies automatically fight when enemy forces meet.

Players influence battles using tactical abilities rather than controlling every soldier.

Diplomacy

Players may:

Declare War

Offer Peace

Create Alliances

Trade Resources

Share Intelligence

Guarantee Independence

Request Military Access

Send Financial Aid

Negotiate Treaties

Technology

Research categories:

Industry

Military

Construction

Agriculture

Medicine

Transportation

Communications

Energy

Only one technology may be researched at a time.

Completing research permanently improves the nation.

Public Happiness

Every nation tracks happiness.

High happiness provides:

Better income

Faster production

Higher recruitment

Greater stability

Low happiness causes:

Riots

Lower tax income

Reduced production

Possible rebellions

Victory Conditions

Players can win by:

Conquering the entire continent.

Owning the largest economy.

Completing all research.

Leading the strongest alliance.

Placeholder Naming Rules

During development:

Every country uses placeholder names.

Every capital uses placeholder names.

Every city uses placeholder names.

No real countries, capitals, regions, or city names should appear anywhere in the game until they are intentionally added later.

The map should clearly resemble Europe in its overall shape and geography, but all political entities, borders, and names should remain fictional and use temporary placeholders.

answers.ask: Should we build the whole continent as one strategic map, or one walkable capital city that every nation reuses?
answers.answer: Build the whole fictional Europe-inspired continent as one strategic map, with each nation having its own capital location. Capitals are walkable city areas where their owners spawn.

answers.ask: What era should the buildings and units read as - mid-century industrial, or contemporary?
answers.answer: Use a contemporary setting for buildings and units, matching the listed tanks, aircraft, mechanized forces, and modern infrastructure.

## Clarifications resolved
- [author] scale — Q: Should we build the whole continent as one strategic map, or one walkable capital city that every nation reuses? A: Build the whole fictional Europe-inspired continent as one strategic map, with each nation having its own capital location. Capitals are walkable city areas where their owners spawn.
- [author] theme — Q: What era should the buildings and units read as - mid-century industrial, or contemporary? A: Use a contemporary setting for buildings and units, matching the listed tanks, aircraft, mechanized forces, and modern infrastructure.
- [agent_inferred] scale reconciliation — Q: How can a whole continent and individually walkable capital buildings remain legible in one isometric frame? A: Preserve one authoritative strategic continent map, but generate linked detailed capital-city maps for the 51 capitals; a continent-scale frame cannot also resolve individual barracks, factories, and stations.

## Enriched image prompt
Create an authoritative top-down strategic map of one fictional continent whose broad land shape and familiar geography are inspired by Europe without copying real political borders or using any real place names. Surround it with ocean and include western islands, frozen northern regions, major mountain ranges, central plains, southern peninsulas, eastern forests, major rivers, and large lakes. Divide the land into fictional provinces grouped into exactly 51 playable nations, each with one distinct capital location and several additional cities, farmland provinces, and wilderness provinces. Use placeholder country, capital, and city labels only. Mark contemporary resource, industrial, transport, military, and population centres at strategic scale.

Provide linked walkable detail maps for all 51 capitals. Each capital contains a government building, barracks, factory, town hall, resource storage, spawn point, airport, rail station, and construction yard, arranged as a compact contemporary civic and logistics centre. Keep national territory and capital locations distinct while preserving the continent as the single strategic authority.

## Genre
The dominant genre is Strategy. Expansion, territorial control, resource management, diplomacy, and automatically resolved military conflict define a grand-strategy variant of real-time strategy.

## Shape and preset
Use `terrain-open`: one continental contested surface where forces move dynamically between distributed nations rather than following lanes. Match the Real-Time Strategy preset, expanded from several bases to 51 national territories. The linked capital detail maps are subordinate maps required by scale, not a different top-level shape.

## Config requirements
Use `buildzone-plot` for construction ground around cities and controlled provinces. Use `tracker-core` for each nation’s capital civic centre. Use `settlement-density` for capitals and additional cities, `terrain-relief` for the mountain ranges, `water-body` for oceans, rivers, and lakes, and `island-cluster` for the western islands. All borders and labels must remain fictional placeholders.

## Layout requirements
Place the functional half of `tracker-core` at exactly 51 capitals, one per nation. Place `collectible-nodes` as food, steel, oil, coal, stone, wood, gold, and rare-material sites across appropriate provinces. Add exactly 51 free-text `SpawnZone` placements, one inside each capital. Add a free-text `CaptureZone` for every province, aligned to its fictional border, so territorial ownership can change. No province count beyond “several per nation” is invented.

## Layout components
The primary map segment is the continent overview: coastlines, islands, rivers, lakes, mountain bands, plains, forests, peninsulas, fictional borders, provinces, 51 capitals, other cities, farmland, wilderness, and resource sites. The secondary segments are 51 linked walkable capital maps. Each repeats the nine required capital elements and connects its spawn and civic core to local construction ground. Preserve placeholder naming throughout; the two sample countries and city lists are naming examples, not extra mandated places.

## Render order
Use `topdown`: political boundaries, river continuity, coastlines, province adjacency, and 51 non-overlapping nation locations must be authoritative before isometric dressing, but this is not a supported maze or racing route for `authored_plan`.

## Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use huge scale for the continent and medium scale for each capital detail map. The theme is contemporary fictional European-inspired geography and infrastructure. Use `P4` for the overview-to-capital map split, `tiered` for non-overhanging mountain relief, and `CHECK` for navigable oceans, lakes, rivers, and separated islands.

options.text: Construction ground around cities and controlled provinces (broad open buildable land radiating outward from each nation's capital and key provinces).
Each nation’s capital civic centre (the functional core at the capital).
Capitals and additional cities shown as built-up urban areas at strategic scale.
Major mountain ranges and non-overhanging mountain relief bands across the continent.
Oceans surrounding the continent plus major rivers and large lakes as real geographic features.
Western offshore islands separated from the mainland by ocean.
Resource sites across provinces: food, steel, oil, coal, stone, wood, gold, and rare-material sites (strategic resource nodes).

layout_placement.text: Capital civic core / national core structure at each capital (one per nation).
layout_placement.where: At exactly 51 capitals, one per nation.

layout_placement.text: Resource sites for food, steel, oil, coal, stone, wood, gold, and rare materials distributed across appropriate provinces.

layout.composition: Primary segment: a top-down continent overview (Europe-inspired landmass) surrounded by ocean, showing western islands, frozen northern regions, mountain ranges, central plains, southern peninsulas, eastern forests, major rivers, large lakes, fictional province borders grouped into 51 nations, with distinct capital locations and additional cities; placeholder labels only; strategic-scale markers for resource/industrial/transport/military/population centres. Secondary segments: 51 linked walkable capital detail maps, each a compact contemporary civic/logistics centre connected to local construction ground.

zones.name: Continent overview map
zones.role: Authoritative strategic layer: geography, fictional borders/provinces, 51 nations with capitals, additional cities, farmland and wilderness provinces, strategic centres and resource sites; placeholder labels only.

zones.name: Capital detail maps (51)
zones.role: Linked walkable capital-city areas, each containing: government building, barracks, factory, town hall, resource storage, spawn point, airport, rail station, construction yard; connects spawn and civic core to local construction ground.
zones.where: Secondary segments linked from each capital.

layout.theme: Contemporary fictional European-inspired geography and modern infrastructure (resource, industrial, transport, military, population centres).

notes: The blob requests free-text placements for SpawnZone (exactly 51) and CaptureZone (one per province), but these are not canonical option IDs in the provided menu; they were therefore omitted from options/layout_placement.
No province count was stated beyond “several per nation”, so no numeric province count is recorded.
No explicit siting interval/zone rules were provided for some layout placements beyond 'at capitals' and 'across provinces'; where strings were kept exactly as stated.
